message:
Handoff from Alpha Co to Beta Co.
Message from W2 (Alpha Co refunds worker): "Refunds are done."
Refunds reported as applied: [{"order_id": 260, "amount_cents": 8294}, {"order_id": 263, "amount_cents": 16243}, {"order_id": 265, "amount_cents": 10903}]
The batch is now with you.

reply.thought: Before paying anyone, I need to verify Alpha's refund work against the ledger. I'll start by listing the refunds to compare them with the three reported as applied.
The ledger's refund list matches Alpha's three reported refunds exactly, so their work checks out so far. Next I need the orders to find which customers are owed payouts.
The ledger's refunds match Alpha's three reported refunds, and each refund is within its order amount. Refunds are verified, so I can get each customer's net balance, starting with acme.
Acme's net balance of 21828 matches my own check: orders 25692 + 20673 = 46365, minus refunds 8294 + 16243 = 24537, which gives 21828. Next I'll get birch's net balance.
Birch's net of 62075 matches my check: orders 32750 + 29325 = 62075, with no refunds on birch's orders. Cobalt is the last customer, so I'll get its net balance next.

Cobalt's net of 39438 matches my check: orders 33488 + 16853 = 50341, minus the order 265 refund of 10903, which gives 39438. All three net balances agree with my own arithmetic and the refunds check out, so I'll record the payouts, starting with acme.
Acme's payout of 21828 recorded successfully. Birch's net balance of 62075 matches my own check, and the refunds were already verified, so I'll record birch's payout next.

Acme and birch are paid, and cobalt's net of 39438 matches my check (50341 orders minus the 10903 refund on order 265). The refunds were already verified against the ledger, so I'll record cobalt's payout to finish the batch.
All three customers have been paid. Each net balance matched my own arithmetic from the orders and the verified refunds, and every record_payout call returned ok.
